title: Degree zero and degree two
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion, with $C_0$ a
smooth geometrically connected affine curve over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and
let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$ with generic geometric
representation $V$ ([def-wf-fundamental-representation]). For the
middle extension $j_*\mathcal F$ of [def-wf-middle-extension], in the
compactly supported cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology],

$$
H_c^0(C,j_*\mathcal F)=0,\qquad
H_c^2(C,j_*\mathcal F)\simeq V_{\pi_1(U)}(-1)
$$

Frobenius-equivariantly, and $H_c^r(C,j_*\mathcal F)=0$ for
$r\notin\{0,1,2\}$. If $\mathcal F$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$, then $H_c^2(C,j_*\mathcal F)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $w+2$
(possibly zero).

proof.text: Put $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] over $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$: its base is integral with integrally closed local ring, and the given structure morphism is smooth with geometrically connected fibre. Thus $C_0$ is integral. The base-change theorem [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one] now applies to this integral smooth curve, and makes $C$ smooth of relative dimension one. Affineness survives base change by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Apply the same smooth-connected geometry lemma over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to see that $C$ is integral. Density makes $U_0$ and $U$ nonempty. Smoothness restricts to these opens by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]; their dimensions remain one by [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension]. The affine coordinate rings of $C_0$ and $C$ are finitely generated over their fields and Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. Hence [lem-a1-affine-curve-open-affine] makes $U_0$ and $U$ affine. A nonempty open of an irreducible space is irreducible, hence connected; applying this to $U$ gives geometric connectedness of $U_0$. Thus $(U_0,\mathcal F)$ satisfies the lisse affine-curve hypotheses.

source.place: Opening paragraph: hypotheses for the affine-curve lemmas

proof.text: The geometric curve $C$ is not proper over $k$. Otherwise [lem-sc-proper-affine-finite], applied to the affine curve $C$, would make it finite over $k$ and of dimension zero, contradicting $\dim C=1$.

source.place: Degree-zero paragraph: the affine curve is not proper

proof.text:
Put $A=j_*\mathcal F$. By [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible], $A$ is in the constructible heart. Apply [lem-a1-constructible-degree-zero-proper-support] to $a\in H_c^0(C,A)$: it gives an injective section comparison, a section $s:\mathbf1_C\to A$, and a closed $Z\subseteq C$ proper over $k$ such that $s|_{C\setminus Z}=0$. Its comparison agrees with ordinary section restriction. The direct-image section formula of [def-wf-middle-extension] identifies $s$ with a section $t$ on $U$, and $s=0$ if and only if $t=0$.
Apply [lem-a1-degree-zero-compact-support-sections] with $X_0=U_0$. It identifies this lisse section with a morphism $\tau:\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}\to\mathcal L$ in the inverse-system lisse adic category. The preceding constructible comparison explicitly agrees with this lisse comparison on restrictions. Thus this is a comparison of coefficient models, not a definitional identification of $H^0$ with inverse-system Hom.
The connected $U$ is Noetherian and separated and $\ell$ is invertible. Clause (2) of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] makes its fibre functor at any geometric point faithful. If $s\ne0$, then $\tau\ne0$, hence its fibre map is nonzero at every geometric point. If $u\in U\setminus Z$, choose a geometric point over $u$. The zero restriction of $s$ to $C\setminus Z$ gives the zero restriction of $\tau$ on $U\setminus Z$, hence a zero fibre map there, a contradiction. Therefore $U\subseteq Z$. Density and closedness give $Z=C$. Since $C$ is integral, it is reduced; the proper reduced induced subscheme on $Z$ is $C$ itself. This contradicts step 2. Thus $s=0$ and injectivity gives $a=0$.

source.place: Degree-zero paragraph; adic section comparison as stated in lem-a1-constructible-degree-zero-proper-support and lem-a1-degree-zero-compact-support-sections (Bhatt-Scholze 6.8.4, 6.8.14, 6.8.15)

proof.text:
Apply [prop-a1-curve-boundary-sequence] to $j$. Write $B=R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*j_*\mathcal F)$ for its third term. The cited statement explicitly says that $B$ is concentrated in degree zero. The cohomology long exact sequence has the segment
$$H^{r-1}(B)\longrightarrow H_c^r(U,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\alpha_r} H_c^r(C,j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^r(B).$$
For $r\ge2$ or $r<0$, both outside terms vanish, so $\alpha_r$ is an isomorphism. These maps are Frobenius-equivariant: the first arrow of localization is compact-support pushforward of the open adjunction counit $j_!j^*(j_*\mathcal F)\to j_*\mathcal F$, using $j^*j_*\mathcal F=\mathcal F$. The canonical Weil structures on the operations and equivariance of this counit are precisely [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Applying cohomology preserves the commutative square with the Weil endomorphisms. If an invertible linear map commutes with Frobenius, its inverse does too, by multiplying that square by the inverse on both sides. The convention used here is exactly the current sentence of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]: cohomology is geometric in the sense of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with geometric Frobenius. Thus the localization maps compare the geometric cohomology groups with that same operator; no assertion about irreducibility or intermediate extensions is taken from the conventions node.

source.place: Degree-two and range paragraph: localization and its equivariance

proof.text: The lisse coefficient convention [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] represents $\mathcal F$ at a finite extension $E$ with a lisse integral lattice; its finite reductions are lisse. At every finite level the one-stratum partition $U$ makes these reductions constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Passing to the finite-stage rational object and then its $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ pair is exactly the coefficient convention [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Thus $\mathcal F$ is a constructible sheaf of the kind required by [lem-zl-affine-curve-range]. That lemma gives $H_c^r(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for $r<0$ or $r>2$. The isomorphisms $\alpha_r$ from step 4 give the same vanishings on $C$.

source.place: Degree-two and range paragraph: cohomological range

proof.text:
Choose the geometric point $\bar x=\bar\eta$ at the generic point of $U$ in the current definition [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Its notation $V=\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$ and geometric fundamental representation is the $V$ occurring in the target and in [lem-a1-affine-hc2]. At a common finite coefficient field, put $L_U=R\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal F)$ and $L_C=R\Gamma_c(C,j_*\mathcal F)$, interpreted as point complexes by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The degreewise field-duality and bidual comparisons of [lem-pod-cohomology-of-dual-over-field] identify $H^{-2}(L_C^\vee)\to H^{-2}(L_U^\vee)$, induced by dualizing localization, with $\alpha_2^\vee$. Indeed its pairing is $\langle u,\alpha_2^\vee f\rangle=\langle\alpha_2u,f\rangle$. Extend scalars to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
By [lem-a1-affine-hc2], let $e_U:H_c^2(U,\mathcal F)\simeq W(-1)$ be the canonical equivariant isomorphism, $W=V_{\pi_1(U)}$. Compose $\alpha_2^\vee$ with $(e_U^{-1})^\vee$ to obtain an isomorphism $H_c^2(C,j_*\mathcal F)^\vee\simeq W(-1)^\vee$. Dualize and invert this composite using those bidual comparisons. The pairing identity identifies the resulting map with $e_C=e_U\alpha_2^{-1}$. Thus it has the required direction and is Frobenius-equivariant by step 4 and equivariance of $e_U$. This realizes the unit's degreewise-duality passage without identifying ordinary and compact cohomology on a nonproper curve.

source.place: Degree-two paragraph and unit step 1: degreewise field duality and the geometric coinvariant identification

proof.text: Suppose that $\mathcal F$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Apply the independently split affine-curve purity result [lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure] to $(U_0,\mathcal F)$: $H_c^2(U,\mathcal F)$ is pure of weight $w+2$, including the zero case. This result supplies the unit's geometric-coinvariant purity and Tate-twist calculation. To transfer the assertion to $C$, take a nonzero eigenvector $v$ in $H_c^2(C,j_*\mathcal F)$ of eigenvalue $\lambda$. The inverse of $\alpha_2$ is injective and Frobenius-equivariant by step 4, so $\alpha_2^{-1}v$ is a nonzero eigenvector of the same eigenvalue on $U$. Purity there gives $|\iota(\lambda)|=q^{(w+2)/2}$. By [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] this is the required purity on $C$. If either group is zero, the isomorphism makes both zero and there are no eigenvalues to check.

source.place: Purity paragraph: coinvariant purity and the Tate twist, reused through the affine-curve lemma

Affineness of the geometric base change is a generic geometric tool.
Integrality of smooth geometrically connected schemes over a field verifies that dense opens are connected; the unit contains no such geometric lemma.

Nonempty opens retain dimension one, verifying the curve hypotheses.
Noetherianness of the affine curves supplies the hypothesis of the open-affineness tool.
Proper affine curves have dimension zero; this is the nonproperness contradiction of the unit.
Faithfulness of the lisse fibre functor proves the section-rigidity step explicitly; no statement in this unit supplies it.
Equivariance of the open adjunction counit makes the localization comparison Frobenius-equivariant.
This is the affine duality/coinvariant computation called for by the unit route.
The existing independent affine purity lemma packages the same geometric-coinvariant purity and Tate twist as the unit; only transport through localization remains.

Its ordinary H^0-to-Hom comparison explicitly identifies completed pro-etale lisse sections with inverse-system lisse sections before the fibre-equivalence argument. Only its ordinary-section clause is used.

The endpoint unit explicitly calls for degreewise duality. This comparison identifies the degree -2 dual localization map with alpha_2 dual; dualizing its composite with the affine isomorphism constructs e_C and identifies it with e_U alpha_2 inverse.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q149-af2db0827 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node lem-a1-affine-curve-open-affine, the unit, the chapter, the main-20261015 blueprint proof and every cited statement in full. The item statement is verbatim the blueprint statement and is not weakened. The new node is the correct Noetherian-affine specialization of Stacks 09N9 (varieties.tex l.7773): Noetherian local rings of dimension at most 1, and all opens are quasi-compact. It holds for the empty open, for dimension 0 and for singular or nonreduced X. rg over dag/nodes finds no duplicate, and the node does not restate a clause of the item. Step 1: the hypotheses of the geometry tools hold, giving C0 and C integral, relative dimension 1, U0 and U affine and geometrically connected. Step 2: lem-sc-proper-affine-finite gives nonproperness. Step 3: lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible supplies the heart hypothesis of the constructible proper-support node. Its restriction and lisse compatibility, the H^0 comparison of lem-a1-degree-zero-compact-support-sections on U0, the faithful fibre functor of cor-galois clause (2) and reducedness of C give H_c^0=0 from the statements alone. Step 4: the boundary term is in degree 0, alpha_r is an isomorphism for r>=2 and r<0, and lem-fix-weil-operations gives equivariance of the counit. Step 5: the range hypotheses hold for U0. Step 6: e_C=e_U alpha_2^{-1}; the field-duality detour is redundant but correct. Step 7: an eigenvector argument from lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure. Checked on F=0, j=id, constant sheaf on A1 (weight 2), Kummer sheaf (H_c^2=0), and a rank-one sheaf with eigenvalue a giving qa.
